cards.title: Figure-consistent driven-qubit GKSL generator

checks.reason: The four-component Supplemental matrix and Supplemental component equations uniquely define this doubled-rate GKSL generator and are the equations used by every theory figure.
The commutator and both GKSL dissipators are trace preserving; positive printed rates make the map completely positive.
For Omega=0 and alpha>0 the up-state population decays to the down state while coherences vanish.

cards.numerical_form: Construct the 4x4 column-vectorized Liouvillian from H=Omega*sigma_x/2 and collapse operators sqrt(2*alpha*gamma)*sigma_minus and sqrt(2*(1-alpha)*gamma)*projector_up; expose the literal Main Eq. (1)-(2) rates separately as a falsification comparator.
open_questions: Main Eqs. (1)-(2), with the paper's explicitly standard dissipator convention, contain rates smaller by exactly two than the Supplemental matrix/Bloch equations. The theory figures follow the Supplemental convention. This is retained as an inconclusive paper-consistency discrepancy pending fresh review.
A main-text experimental paragraph separately writes H=Omega*sigma_x, whereas Main Eq. (1), the Supplemental matrix, and the standard Rabi convention require H=Omega*sigma_x/2.

cards.title: Affine Bloch-vector dynamics
cards.latex: \dot x=-\gamma x,\qquad \dot y=-\gamma y-\Omega z,\qquad \dot z=\Omega y-2\alpha\gamma(1+z)

checks.reason: Supplement Eqs. (3)-(6) explicitly define the Bloch coordinates and all three affine ODE components.
Substituting rho=(I+x sigma_x+y sigma_y+z sigma_z)/2 into EQ001 yields every printed component and affine term.
Bloch propagation will be checked pointwise against a separately assembled 4x4 density-matrix Liouvillian.
The x component decouples and decays exactly as exp(-gamma t), matching the printed lambda_x mode.

cards.numerical_form: For Omega=1 use A=[[-gamma,-1],[1,-2*alpha*gamma]] and b=[0,-2*alpha*gamma] on r2=(y,z).

cards.title: Steady state and elliptical locus

source_refs.value: Main Fig. 2 left and Supplement Fig. 2

checks.reason: Supplement Eqs. (5)-(8) print the steady state, dimensionless form, and ellipse identity used by the figures.
Solving A r* + b=0 gives the displayed rational functions and eliminating gamma' gives the ellipse identity.
The paper-scale runner requires max norm of A r*+b below 1e-12 across every figure grid.
gamma' to zero approaches the Bloch-sphere origin; gamma' to infinity approaches the south pole.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the closed rational functions directly in float64 and cross-check against a linear solve of the affine fixed-point equation.

cards.title: Relaxation rates, modes, and bifurcation

checks.reason: Main Eq. (4) and Supplemental Eqs. (9)-(10) specify the eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and left-mode definition.
The roots of det(A-lambda I) give the printed pair; the discriminant vanishes at gamma'_b.
Analytic rates will be compared to numpy.linalg.eigvals of the Bloch generator across and on both sides of the bifurcation.
For alpha in [0,1] and positive gamma', every nonzero mode has nonpositive real part.

cards.numerical_form: Use complex square roots below the bifurcation and record real parts; label lambda_plus as the fast branch (more negative above the bifurcation) and lambda_minus as the slow branch.

cards.title: Slow-mode amplitude and strong inverse-Mpemba initial state

checks.reason: The paper gives both the explicit a_- expression and the closed strong-effect initial temperature.
Substitution of gamma'_{i,SME} into Supplemental Eq. (11) cancels the slow amplitude.
A separate dual-eigenvector projection of the initial displacement must have a slow component below 1e-11 at the same root.
alpha=0.94 and gamma'_f=15 give gamma'_{i,SME}=0.0761974279, consistent with the paper's approximately 0.07.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate Supplemental Eq. (11) for the displayed paper normalization; independently solve the two-mode decomposition only to verify the invariant zero and sign change.
open_questions: A modal coefficient depends on eigenvector normalization; the plotted absolute a_- follows Supplemental Eq. (11), while physical zero crossings and products a_n v_n are normalization invariant.

cards.title: Exact relaxation, distance, crossing, and maximum advantage

source_refs.value: Main Eq. (3) and definition of d_ss

checks.reason: Main Eq. (3), the d_ss definition, and Supplement Sec. 3 explicitly define the propagated state, distance crossing, and post-crossing comparison.
Subtracting the final fixed point removes the affine term, leaving the exact homogeneous matrix exponential.
Bloch-space distances will be compared with density matrices propagated by the independent 4x4 Liouvillian.
Crossings are bracketed before Brent solving, and maximal post-crossing advantage is checked against a dense-grid maximum.
For alpha=0.94, gamma'_f=15, gamma'_{i,H}=0.77, the crossing-time minimum lies near gamma'_{i,SME} and the maximum advantage is about 0.084, matching Supplement Fig. 5.

cards.numerical_form: Set Omega=1, evaluate scipy.linalg.expm(A*t), solve the first nontrivial sign change with scipy.optimize.brentq, and maximize d_H-d_C with bounded scalar optimization.

cards.title: Steady-state pure-state mixture for direct preparation

checks.reason: The main text and Supplemental paragraph after Eq. (8) print p, theta, the pure states, and mixture weights.
p=sqrt(y*^2+z*^2) and theta=atan2(z*,y*) reduce to the printed expressions.
The analytic steady-state locus stays inside the Bloch sphere, so 0<=p<=1 and both mixture weights are probabilities.

cards.numerical_form: Compute p and theta from the independently evaluated steady state; this is a consistency check only because the Main Fig. 5 experimental arrays are unavailable.

cards.title: Literal main-text GKSL rates used as a falsification comparator

source_refs.value: Main Eqs. (1)-(2) and the printed definition of L_A

checks.reason: The rates and standard dissipator normalization are printed unambiguously together in Main Eqs. (1)-(2).
Direct expansion gives dot y=-(gamma/2)y-Omega z and dot z=Omega y-alpha gamma(1+z), exactly half the dissipative coefficients of Supplement Eq. (4).

At fixed printed gamma'=gamma/Omega, its steady-state locus equals the Supplemental locus evaluated at gamma'/2, producing a factor-two temperature-axis mismatch rather than a numerical-solver ambiguity.

cards.numerical_form: Construct a second 4x4 Liouvillian with sqrt(alpha*gamma) and sqrt((1-alpha)*gamma) collapse amplitudes; use it only for discrepancy quantification, never as the figure generator.
open_questions: The most economical correction is to insert a factor two in both Main Eq. (2) rates, but lifecycle classification requires fresh inventory-first review and explicit alternative-explanation falsification.
